items.title: Gluing finitely many finite local extensions along the height one primes of a two-dimensional local ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology), section on the key lemma for the tame symbol
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma glues finitely many finite local extensions A_{q_i} contained in B_i, each with B_i/A_{q_i} killed by a power of t, into a single finite extension A contained in B of local rings with B_{q_i} isomorphic to B_i and B/A killed by a power of t (statement lines 1106-1114). The construction is not a direct limit: denominators have to be bounded once and for all by choosing n with B_i contained in t^{-n}A_{q_i}, and the two-step choice of M contained in t^{-2n}A and then of the subring B = A + m^{c+1}M is what forces both the prescribed localizations and the finite generation over the two-dimensional local ring (proof lines 1118-1128). The closing verification that B is local with maximal ideal m + m^{c+1}M is explicitly left unstated by the author, and is reproduced as written. The claim is H2: the argument is short but the two nested bounded-denominator modules are a genuine construction rather than a citation.
